The core signal logic (DI+ vs DI- crossover) is simple enough for manual Python reimplementation once the custom ADX Smoothed indicator logic is replicated.

position_sizing.conditional_logic: If MM<0 then MM is treated as fixed lot size; if MM>0 then MM is share of deposit

custom_logic_notes: The entry signal uses a two-bar comparison: at bar index SignalBar=1, compares DI+/DI- on current and previous bar. BUY_Open triggers when DiPlus[1]>DiMinus[1] (current bar DI+ > DI-) AND DiPlus[0]<=DiMinus[0] (previous bar DI+ <= DI-), i.e. DI+ freshly crossed above DI-. SELL_Open triggers symmetrically. Position close on opposite signal is independent of open permission flags. The Recount flag ensures signals are recalculated if CopyBuffer fails. The custom ADX_Smoothed indicator applies double smoothing (alpha1=0.25, alpha2=0.33) to standard ADX DI+ and DI- lines; this smoothing algorithm must be reverse-engineered from the indicator source for Python conversion.
external_dependencies: TradeAlgorithms.mqh - provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, LoadHistory, GlobalVariableDel_, CIsNewBar
ADX_Smoothed custom indicator - provides smoothed DI+ and DI- buffers
python_conversion_notes: 1. Must reimplement ADX_Smoothed custom indicator: likely applies Ehrlich multiplicator or double exponential smoothing to standard ADX DI+/DI- with alpha1=0.25 and alpha2=0.33. Source code of ADX_Smoothed indicator needed to replicate exactly. 2. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides standard position open/close wrappers - these are straightforward market order execution with SL/TP and deviation checks, easily replicated in Python. 3. Position sizing: MM=-0.1 means fixed 0.1 lot; if positive, represents deposit fraction requiring equity-based lot calculation. 4. Entry is DI+/DI- crossover on H4 bars, evaluated once per new bar. 5. SL=1000 points, TP=2000 points (at 5-digit broker: SL=100 pips, TP=200 pips). 6. Signal reversal closes opposite positions before opening new ones. 7. The SignalBar=1 parameter means signals are read from the completed bar (index 1), avoiding repainting.
